core.text: The Tortoise Trainer was painted in 1906 by Osman Hamdi Bey, a leading Ottoman painter and archaeologist.
An elderly man in a long robe tries to train a group of tortoises, which slowly go their own way.

detail.text: The scene is usually said to be set in an upper room of the Green Mosque in Bursa.
Many viewers read the painting as gentle satire on the slow pace of reform; the face of the trainer is often compared with the painter's own.
Today the painting is in the collection of the Pera Museum in Istanbul.
